The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No. LAQ / ARB /
NH-4(BET) / 09 / 2012-13, 08/2012-13 and 125/2010-11 dated 06.08.2021 pertaining to Sy. No.99 measuring 426 Sq. Meters (142 Sq. Meters each belongs to respondents 1 to 3) of Medahalli village.

.2. The definite case of the petitioner is that the property of respondents 1 to 3 measuring 142 Square Meters each (total 426 Square Meters) in Survey No. 99 of Medahalli village has been acquired under Preliminary Notification dated 14.12.2006 and Final Notification dated 14.11.2007.

The respondent No.5 has passed the award on 11.08.2008 determined the market value of the land at Rs.1,111.95 per Square Meters and awarded a total compensation amount of Rs.1,57,897/-, which has been received by the A.P. No.13/2023 respondents 1 to 3 each towards 142 Square Meters of land under protest.

Subsequently, on 08.10.2012 the respondents 1 to 3 have filed separate National Highway Authority Of India vs Purushottam H Patel on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119700277/
2 application to fix the compensation of Rs.6,000/- per Square feet each in respect of 142 Square Meters each.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the applications are taken by the respondent No.5 for consideration.

.3. Thereafter, the Arbitrator hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ / ARB / NH-4(BET)
/ 09/08/2012-13 and 125/2010-11 dated 06.08.2021.
.4.
Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting aside the following:

:GROUNDS:
The petitioner claims that the impugned is perverse, patently illegal, capricious and goes against the very fundamentals of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

Further, the award passed by the  A.P. No.13/2023 respondent No.5 on 11.08.2008 but the respondents approached the respondent No.4 seeking enhancement of compensation only on 08.10.2012 i.e., after a lapse of more than 4 years from the date of passing of award by the respondent No.5 and hence, the claim of the respondents 1 and 2 was barred by time.
Further there is no finding or reasons recorded on the aspect of limitation or as to how the claims of respondent 1 and 2 were maintainable.
The respondent No.4 ought to have followed Section 3-G(7)(a) of the NH Act.

Contrary to Section 3-G 7(a) of the NH Act, the respondent No.4 has relied upon the guidance value notification No.
IGR/CVC/5/2006-07 dated 17.04.2007 which has came into effect from 19.04.2007 i.e., subsequent to the Preliminary Notification which was published in the year 2006 and the very basis for enhancing the compensation was based upon a document which was not even in existence as on the date of Preliminary Notification but absolutely A.P. No.13/2023 there is no reason assigned for placing reliance upon the notification dated 17.04.2007.

Further submits that placing reliance upon a subsequent notification and taking the guidance value of Rs. 2,100/- per Square Meters as the basis, the respondent No.4 directly in the operative portion of the added a percentage of 50% on the ground that the subject lands were abutting National Highway and thereafter added an addition percentage of 25 towards enhancement and arrived at Rs. 1,48,75,000/- per acre i.e., Rs.
3,676/- per Sq. Meters (Rs. 85 lakhs per acre i.e., Rs. 1,111.95 per Sq.
Meters + Rs. 42,50,000/- per acre i.e., 50% of Rs. 85 lakhs + Rs. 21,25,000/- per acre i.e., 25% of Rs. 85 lakhs = Rs. 1,48,75,000/- per acre.

Further the respondent No.4 failed to follow the procedure laid down in Section 24 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act Among other grounds,
prayed for relief claimed in the petition.

Perused the materials on record, on that basis my findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 : In the affirmative Point No.2 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS .8. POINT No.1:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The respondents 1 to 3 are the owners of the property bearing Sy. No.99 measuring to A.P. No.13/2023 an extent of 142 Square Meters each (total 426 Sq. Meters) of Medahalli village and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-4 under Preliminary Notification dated 14.12.2006 and Final Notification dated 14.11.2007,
is an admitted fact.

It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the respondent No.5/Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India being a SLAO determined the compensation at Rs.1111.95 per Square meter for the acquired land.

It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs. 1,57,897/-
was disbursed to the respondents 1 to 3 each as compensation.

.9. Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the respondents 1 to 3 have separately filed an application as on 08.10.2012 to fix the compensation of Rs.6,000/- per Square feet each in respect of 142 Square Meters each.
Accordingly, the application is taken by the respondent No.5 for consideration.

On basis of the said application, the A.P. No.13/2023 respondent No.5 hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ/ARB/NH-4 (BET) 09/08/2012-13 &
125/2010-11 dated 06.08.2021.
The respondent No.4 in its order enhanced the compensation from Rs.1,111.95 Sq. Meters to 3,676/- per Sq. Meters.

sentences.text: The said enhancement has been challenged by the petitioner in this petition.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent No.4 without considering the relevant provisions of NHA Act and also without considering the guidance value or market value of the property as on the date of Preliminary Notification enhanced the compensation by relying on the guidance value of the year 2007 published vide notification bearing No. IGR/CVC/05/2006-07 dated 17.04.2007.
The petitioner also claimed that the Preliminary Notification was published as on 14.12.2006.

As such,
the respondent No. 5 ought to have considered the market value of the property of the year 2006 and not of the year 2007.
As the aforesaid notification relied by the Arbitrator came to effect from 17.04.2007 i.e., after A.P. No.13/2023 lapse of more than 4 months from the date of publication of Preliminary Notification.
Accordingly claimed that the said enhancement cannot be accepted.
It is true that as per the NH Act, the market value of the land as on the date of Preliminary Notification has to be considered.

.11. In the case on hand, Subsequent to the notification bearing No.
IGR/CVC/05/2006-07 dated 17.04.2007, the circular order not produced.
The LAO enhanced the compensation arbitrarily.

During the course of argument it is argued by the counsel for the petitioner that the arbitrator enhanced the compensation from Rs.1,111.95 to Rs.2,564/- per square meter and the said enhancement is to the extent of almost more than two times of the compensation awarded by the LAO.
.12.
Now it is for the consideration of this court to see that whether the said enhancement is supported with any materials or is there any reasons given by the Arbitrator for the said enhancement.

It appears from A.P. No.13/2023 the award that the Arbitrator enhanced the compensation on the basis of notification bearing No. IGR/CVC/05/2006-07 dated 17.04.2007 which is subsequent to the preliminary notification.

On perusal of records of arbitration proceedings, it is clear that the notification bearing No. IGR/CVC/05/2006-07 dated 17.04.2007 is not the part of record and also there is no material on record to show that said notification has been brought to the notice of petitioner before passing of the Award.

In view of the principle laid down by Apex court in a case of Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs. National Highways Authority of India such award cannot be accepted as the notification relied by the Arbitrator is not the part of arbitration proceedings and the same has not been brought to the notice of petitioner before passing the award.

sentences.text: As such opportunity to the petitioner to make submission or give explanation to the said notification has been denied.
As such, certainly this enhancement of respondent No.4/arbitrator cannot be accepted.
In the case on hand, the Arbitrator has enhanced compensation to the tune of 75%.
Of course there is some reason for enhancement of 50%, but there is no reasoning for enhancement of 25% of the compensation amount.
It is simply stated that 25% compensation has been enhanced by using the discretion.
It is well settled principle of law that discretion must be used judiciously and not arbitrarily.

What ever the enhancement has been granted by the Arbitrator,
certainly effect the State or State Exchequer.
Hence, Arbitrator shall give reasons for enhancement of the compensation.

As already stated above, the Arbitrator / respondent No.4 has not given any National Highway Authority Of India vs Purushottam H Patel on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119700277/
5 explanation for enhancement of 25% in addition to 50%.

entities.text: National Highway Authority Of India vs Purushottam H Patel

sentences.text: Hence such enhancement cannot be accepted.

.14. In the case on hand, though the respondent No.5 served with the notice not chosen to appear before the court to resist the case of the petitioner or to support the award passed by the respondent No.4.
Absolutely there is no material placed before the court A.P. No.13/2023 to disbelieve the petitioner case or to substantiate the award passed by the respondent No.4.
Hence, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to intervene with the award passed by the Arbitrator and the award is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, the point No. 1 is held in the affirmative.
.15. Point No.2:
In view of my above finding, I proceed to pass the following.
ORDER  Petition filed under Section  34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act is hereby allowed.

Consequently, the award  passed by the Arbitrator /
 respondent No.4 in case No.
 LAQ/ARB/NH-4 (BET) 09/2012-  13, 08/2012-13 and 125/2010-11 dated 06.08.2021 pertaining to Sy.
No.99 measuring 426 Sq. Meters (142 Sq. Meters each to respondents 1 to 3) of Medahalli village,
Bidarahalli Hobli, K.R. A.P. No.13/2023 Puram Taluk, is set aside with a liberty to the parties to pursue their remedy in accordance with law.
Office is directed to send the Lower Court Records.
